title: [WIP] Fix failing CI unit test for canonical cycle key
body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.


<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Repo: maevnholdingstrust/Apex-Omega-v6
> 
> Goal: Fix failing CI unit test in GitHub Actions job (run 25194635875, job 73872367741) where pytest fails:
> - failing test: python/apex_omega_core/tests/test_expanded_graph_scan.py::TestCanonicalCycleKey::test_two_hop_key
> - assertion error: assert ('A','B') == frozenset({'A','B'})
> 
> Context:
> - The test expects _canonical_cycle_key(["A","B","A"]) to return frozenset({"A","B"}).
> - Current implementation of _canonical_cycle_key returns a tuple for 2-hop cycles.
> 
> Required changes:
> 1. Locate _canonical_cycle_key implementation in python/apex_omega_core/core/expanded_graph_scan.py.
> 2. Update it so that for cycles with exactly two unique tokens (e.g., tokens [A,B,A]) it returns frozenset of the unique tokens, order-independent.
>    - Ensure behavior for 3+ unique-token cycles remains stable and continues to satisfy:
>      - same tokens different order yields same key
>      - different token set yields different key
> 3. Add/adjust any small helper logic needed to robustly determine unique tokens for a cycle (typically tokens[0]==tokens[-1] cycles).
> 4. Run/ensure tests pass.
> 
> Notes:
> - Keep the public API unchanged other than the return type for 2-hop canonical keys.
> - Prefer minimal, targeted change.
> 
> References:
> - Workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cd python && python -m pytest apex_omega_core/tests/ -v --tb=short`.
> - Test file: python/apex_omega_core/tests/test_expanded_graph_scan.py (see lines around 159-174 for canonical key tests).
> 
> Failing logs ref: e777884f78bf484c283a62e3ad133d1ae585ae21
> 
> The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):
> 
> User: Please find a solution for this failing job. Use the logs, job definition, and any referenced files where the failure occurred. Keep your response focused on the solution and include code suggestions when appropriate.
> 
> Assistant: The job is failing due to a single unit test assertion mismatch in `_canonical_cycle_key`:
> 
> - Failing test: `apex_omega_core/tests/test_expanded_graph_scan.py::TestCanonicalCycleKey::test_two_hop_key`
> - Error: `AssertionError: assert ('A', 'B') == frozenset({'A', 'B'})`
> 
> This means `_canonical_cycle_key(["A","B","A"])` is currently returning a **tuple** like `('A','B')`, but the test expects a **frozenset**: `frozenset({"A","B"})`.
> 
> ## Fix (recommended): make `_canonical_cycle_key` return a `frozenset` for 2-hop cycles
> 
> Update the implementation of `_canonical_cycle_key` (in `python/apex_omega_core/core/expanded_graph_scan.py`, imported by the test as `from apex_omega_core.core.expanded_graph_scan import _canonical_cycle_key`) so that when the cycle only contains two unique tokens, it returns `frozenset({token0, token1})`.
> 
> Suggested implementation pattern:
> 
> ```python
> def _canonical_cycle_key(tokens: list[str]):
>     # tokens is a cycle like ["A", "B", "A"] or ["A", "B", "C", "A"]
>     uniq = set(tokens[:-1]) if tokens and tokens[0] == tokens[-1] else set(tokens)
> 
>     # Special-case 2-hop (2 unique tokens): make it order-independent
>     if len(uniq) == 2:
>         return frozenset(uniq)
> 
>     # Otherwise keep existing canonicalization for 3+ unique tokens
>     # (whatever your current logic is for rotation / direction invariance)
>     ...
> ```
> 
> Why this works:
> - The test explicitly wants order-independence for 2-hop cycles and encodes that as a `frozenset`.
> - It also won’t break the other two `_canonical_cycle_key` tests as long as your 3+ token logic remains stable (those tests only require equal/not-equal behavior across permutations).
> 
> ## Alternative fix (not recommended): change the test expectation
> You *could* change the test to accept the tuple output, but the existing suite already encodes the intended API/behavior: two-hop keys are treated as a set-like key. It’s better to align the implementation with that expectation.
> 
> ## Where the failure is
> - Test expectation is at `python/apex_omega_core/tests/test_expanded_graph_scan.py` lines 171–174 (at ref `e777884f78bf484c283a62e3ad133d1ae585ae21`):
>   - `assert key == frozenset({"A", "B"})`
> 
> Once `_canonical_cycle_key` returns a `frozenset` for the 2-hop case, CI should go back to green (the run shows 459 passed, 1 failed).
> 
> User: CREATE A PR FOR THE FULL FIX 
> 
> Assistant: I’ve kicked off the pull request creation with the targeted change to make `_canonical_cycle_key(["A","B","A"])` return `frozenset({"A","B"})`; I’m now waiting for the PR workflow to finish so I can share the PR link and confirm CI is green.
> 
> 


</details>
